concepts.name: Backtracking for Permutations
concepts.description: A recursive algorithm that generates all n! permutations of a list by fixing one position at a time, swapping elements into place, recursing on the remainder, and undoing the swap (backtracking) to restore state before trying the next candidate.

concepts.name: N-Queens Problem
concepts.description: The N-Queens puzzle places N queens on an N×N chessboard so no two share a row, column, or diagonal. Backtracking places exactly one queen per row, using sets to track column and diagonal conflicts in O(1) time, enabling pruning of invalid subtrees.

concepts.name: Power Set Generation
concepts.description: The power set of n elements contains all 2^n subsets. A backtracking approach records a valid subset at every recursive call (since every partial path is valid), then extends it by including each remaining element before backtracking to try alternatives.

concepts.name: Trie (Prefix Tree)
concepts.description: A tree data structure where each edge represents one character, allowing root-to-node paths to spell prefixes. Supports O(k) insertion and lookup for strings of length k, enabling efficient prefix-based queries used in autocomplete and spell-check.

concepts.name: Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union)
concepts.description: A data structure that tracks a partition of n elements into disjoint groups. It supports 'find' and 'union' operations in near-O(1) amortized time using two optimizations: path compression (rewiring nodes directly to root) and union by rank (attaching shallower trees under deeper ones).

concepts.name: Kruskal's Algorithm
concepts.description: A greedy algorithm for finding a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of a weighted graph. It sorts all edges by weight and iteratively adds the cheapest edge that does not create a cycle, using Union-Find to efficiently check connectivity between components.
